SMTO-CFG-0065 — The time limit given for this task isn't a usable number

GUID: 329c859c-5bb6-48ee-8fcd-a5313291ef2d
Slug: wall-budget-invalid
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • SMTO was given a time limit for this task that isn't a usable number of seconds, for example a negative or endless value. The task didn't start or resume with it and stays as it was.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the task and select Resume. The Resume button reuses the task's own saved time limit, so it doesn't send the bad value.
  2. If a script or another tool resumed the task, change its time limit to a whole number of seconds from 0 to 86,400, where 0 means no time limit. SMTO accepts only a real, non-negative number of seconds and caps it at one day.

What success looks like

  • The task shows as running again instead of stopped or paused.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, and say how the task was resumed. Don't change the Model request timeout or command time limits; they are separate from the task's time limit.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • renew_wall_budget rejected an explicitly supplied wall duration that does not convert to a finite, non-negative number, so the run was not started or resumed with it.

What this means

  • An explicitly requested renewed wall duration cannot convert to a finite nonnegative number; valid durations are normalized separately to the supported bound. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • An explicitly requested renewed wall duration cannot convert to a finite nonnegative number; valid durations are normalized separately to the supported bound.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the explicit wall duration for invalid type, negative value or infinity, distinct from absolute deadlines and tool timeouts.

How to fix it

  • Pass wall_seconds (RunControl resume) or native_wall_seconds as a finite number of 0 or more; values are clamped to 1–86400 seconds and 0 disables the wall deadline. Omit it to reuse the run's configured wall_limit_seconds. Keep the task wall budget separate from model request and shell operation timeouts.
  • Supply a finite duration of zero or greater through the supported budget field. Keep task wall budget separate from model request and shell operation timeouts.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported finite nonnegative duration renews the task's owned wall budget.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
